findings.finding: The `` wildcard origin label for Netlify deploy previews is effectively an open-origin hole. Netlify preview hostnames are arbitrary (`<branch>--<site>.netlify.app`), so a label wildcard like `.netlify.app` (or worse, ``) lets any Netlify-hosted site call your Post API through your credentials. Since the proxy is same-origin from the browser's perspective, the CORS layer is your only credential-abuse barrier.
findings.suggestion: Restrict the wildcard to your site's preview pattern specifically (e.g. `--<site-slug>.netlify.app`), confirm the matcher only allows a single wildcard segment, and document that `` alone is rejected by validation. Add a test asserting `https://evil--someone-else.netlify.app` gets 403.  2. Category: dependency — Severity: medium

findings.finding: The plan assumes Bunny standalone Edge Scripts can be created and served via the Compute API without being attached to a pull zone, and that a Bunny-hostname URL is directly callable with an `Origin` check. If standalone scripts require zone attachment or a custom hostname, the deploy script and the "own origin" rule both change shape.
findings.suggestion: Verify this against the Bunny API before writing the deploy script (it's the plan's step-5 probe moved earlier). If a zone is required, note it now — it changes AC5's "own origin" value.  3. Category: risk — Severity: medium

findings.finding: Netlify's proxy (redirect rule with `200!` status) has its own timeout (~10s on the platform). The Post client timeout is 8s, leaving ~2s for OAuth token fetch plus first-token acquisition. First requests after a cold isolate (token fetch + autocomplete) could exceed the Netlify budget and surface as Netlify errors rather than your clean 502.
findings.suggestion: Tune the token fetch timeout as well (e.g. 3s), so worst-case total stays under ~8s, and have the handler degrade to 502 cleanly if the token can't be fetched in time.  4. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: Single-flight token cache is per-isolate; Bunny edge scripts run in multiple isolates, so a burst after cold start can stampede Post's token endpoint (multiple parallel client-credential grants). Not a correctness bug — Post tokens coexist fine — but could hit Post-side rate limits or trigger alarm bells on their side.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable to leave as-is; optionally cache the token in Bunny's per-script storage if it exists, or just note it as a known limitation.  5. Category: risk — Severity: low

findings.finding: AC10 removes `@supabase/supabase-js` and the `supabase/` folder, but the plan doesn't include a verification step that nothing else (auth, other edge functions, env vars in Netlify, `VITE_SUPABASE_` references in code or Netlify config) still references Supabase. A stale import or env reference fails only at build or runtime.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit grep/CI check step (`grep -r supabase src edge netlify.toml`) as part of step 3, and remember to remove Supabase env vars from the Netlify site settings (manual, add to the triage card alongside project deletion).  6. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: The `postcode4` `63`-prefix restriction means the service never returns non-Zug postcodes — good — but AC9's flow (user types a non-Zug postcode and gets the form-level error) depends on the client-side municipality snapshot staying in sync with the service filter. The plan correctly shares `isOfferedLocality`, which mitigates this — just confirm the browser also validates on submit, not only on suggestion pick (AC9 implies it but the file list doesn't name where that check lives).
findings.suggestion: Confirm the submit-time postcode check uses `isOfferedLocality` and has a test; the spec text implies it exists from step 1.  7. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: Rate limiter is fixed-window (60/min per client, 3000/h total). Fixed windows allow 2× bursts at window boundaries, and in-memory state resets on isolate restart — acknowledged as "per-instance" in FR-01.10, so this is documented, but the 3000/h global limit is also per-isolate, meaning the real ceiling is `3000 × N` isolates.
findings.suggestion: Fine for this step; consider noting in the FR text that limits are per-isolate so the number isn't read as a hard guarantee.  Overall assessment: Sound, well-scoped plan with good shared-logic reuse (parser, municipality rule) and a sensible migration path. The two items to resolve before/during implementation are the origin-wildcard scope and confirming Bunny's standalone-script hosting model; everything else is refinement.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: The per-client limiter has no defined client-IP source across Netlify → Bunny. Using the connection address could group visitors under Netlify’s proxy IP; trusting arbitrary forwarded headers could let direct callers bypass limits.
findings.suggestion: Define which platform-supplied IP information is trustworthy on each path and how proxy traffic is authenticated. Test distinct visitors through Netlify and spoofed forwarding headers against Bunny directly. Bound and expire the limiter’s client map.

findings.finding: The eight-second timeout is specified only for autocomplete. OAuth acquisition, waiting for a shared token refresh, and the retry after a 401 can extend the request substantially or leave it waiting indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Apply an overall request deadline covering token acquisition and both autocomplete attempts. Ensure failed token refresh clears the single-flight promise so subsequent requests can recover. Test OAuth timeout and repeated 401 responses.

findings.finding: The preview-origin wildcard is underspecified. A rule accepting arbitrary Netlify preview hosts would allow unrelated deployments to consume the Post quota. Also, browser origin restrictions do not authenticate callers: direct clients can forge `Origin`.
findings.suggestion: Anchor the wildcard to this Netlify site’s exact preview hostname pattern and test deceptive suffixes and unrelated sites. Specify handling of missing and `null` origins, and keep quota protection independent of origin checks.

findings.finding: AC9 requires blocking invoice creation, but the plan only explicitly changes municipality proposals. That does not establish whether a manually entered postcode, or a previously selected municipality followed by an edit, can bypass the restriction.
findings.suggestion: Verify that invoice submission validates the current postcode against the shared offered-locality rule. Add browser coverage for direct entry of an excluded postcode and editing a valid address to an excluded postcode before submission.  The shared handler and staged Netlify proxy rollout are sound and appropriately scoped. Define the proxy trust boundary, complete timeout behavior, and verify the invoice submission guard before proceeding; the supplied workspace contains no source files, so existing implementation safeguards could not be checked.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.suggestion: fixed: streamed read with byte counter, test with ReadableStream; live 413 up to 5 KB, Bunny gateway 502 above ~50 KB

findings.suggestion: fixed: waits for the autocomplete fetch before aborting

findings.suggestion: fixed: entries skipped, token parse failure = PostError token, tests added

findings.suggestion: fixed: falls back to unexpired token, test added

findings.suggestion: fixed: loopback clients only

findings.suggestion: fixed: reset on failure

findings.suggestion: fixed: removed

findings.suggestion: fixed: removed

findings.finding: The esbuild bundle is built with `tsconfig: 'tsconfig.json'`, but the new `tsconfig.edge.json` (which defines the `@/` path alias) is not used. The handler imports `src/lib/municipality.ts`, which imports `@/data/types` (visible in the unchanged import at the top of `municipality.ts`). Typical Vite root `tsconfig.json` files only carry project references, not `paths`, so esbuild will fail to resolve `@/data/types` when bundling for Bunny — and even if the root tsconfig happens to work today, the alias is only guaranteed by the edge tsconfig.
findings.suggestion: Point esbuild at `tsconfig: 'tsconfig.edge.json'` (or add the `@/` paths mapping to the build call), so the bundle resolves the app-internal alias deterministically.

findings.finding: AC5 requires "invalid JSON / fields → 400", but `parseLookupRequest` accepts arbitrary unknown extra fields (e.g. `{"searchTerm":"Dorf","evil":"…"}`). The old Supabase version also validated a `type` field; the new one validates nothing beyond the two known keys, so a body with unexpected fields is passed through as valid. This is a mild loosening versus the spec's "anything unexpected is rejected" contract comment right above it.
findings.suggestion: Reject bodies containing keys other than `searchTerm` and `zipCode` (a simple `Object.keys` check).

findings.finding: The 1 KB limit is enforced by `Content-Length` or by buffering the entire body via `await request.text()` first. A chunked request with no Content-Length (trivial to send) is fully read into memory before the 413 check, so a hostile client can make the instance buffer an arbitrarily large body. Bunny may cap this upstream, but the code itself does not.
findings.suggestion: Stream the body (read chunks with a running byte count and abort at `MAX_BODY_BYTES`), or rely on an explicit platform limit and document it.

findings.finding: import process from 'node:process'` and `process.env[name]` assume the Bunny Edge Scripting runtime exposes Node-style `process.env` for script variables/secrets. This is unverifiable from the diff (the SDK is loaded with `deno` conditions, suggesting a Deno-like runtime). If Bunny exposes variables differently (e.g. via a SDK API), the service would answer 503 for every lookup in production. The smoke test in the deploy script would catch it, but only after publish.
findings.suggestion: Verify during the first deploy that `process.env` actually carries the Bunny variables/secrets (the smoke test asserts `results.length > 0`, which requires a real Post answer, so this is covered — just be aware the publish happens before the check).

findings.finding: The spec/design notes say React list keys come from `street|houseNumber|postcode|town`. The implementation appends `|${index}` and reads the house number via `houseNumbers?.[0]`, making the key effectively positional. Two different suggestion objects at the same index across refetches share a key, and reordering remounts instead of moves. The handler already dedupes, so the index suffix is unnecessary.
findings.suggestion: Drop the `|${index}` suffix (or keep it only as a fallback if the composite key can genuinely collide).

findings.finding: The "does not answer in time" test runs with the default vitest real timers and a 50 ms `lookupTimeoutMs`, plus `now: () => 0` makes the logged duration always 0 — the deadline path is exercised but the "8 s overall budget shared with a 3 s token budget" interaction (token slow, then lookup slow) is never tested at the handler level. The postClient tests cover each deadline in isolation, so this is a gap rather than a false positive.
findings.suggestion: Optionally add a test where the token resolves after 2 s (fake timers) and the autocomplete hangs, asserting one 502 within the total budget.  Verified as sound (no findings): origin policy incl. the exact preview regex and negative cases (suffix/prefix/port/http/other-site all tested); token single-flight, 30 s refresh margin, exactly-one 401 retry; per-instance fixed-window limiter; no body/Post-text in logs (test asserts absence); `Cache-Control: no-store` on every answer incl. errors; dev plugin off under `E2E=1` and reading only `POST_APIM_`; dist secret scan wired into `npm run build`; Supabase fully removed (deps, code, config, docs); `proposeMunicipality` border-village change matches AC9 and the new tests; the changed Bennau behavior is intentional per the updated spec and no stale caller remains.

findings.finding: The dependency changes have no corresponding lockfile update in the supplied diff. A checkout using `npm ci` will fail because the new SDK is absent from the lockfile, and the specification’s requirement to pin it there is unmet.
findings.suggestion: Regenerate and commit the lockfile, including the Supabase removal. Verify installation and required checks from a clean checkout.

findings.finding: request.text()` buffers the entire body before enforcing the 1 KB limit when `Content-Length` is absent or understated. A large chunked request from an allowed origin can consume substantial memory before receiving 413; the rate limiter runs only afterward.
findings.suggestion: Read the request stream with a byte counter and cancel it immediately when it exceeds 1,024 bytes. Add a test for an oversized streamed body without `Content-Length`.  Ship-with-fixes. The service follows most of the specified design, but the dependency lockfile and effective request-size enforcement need correction before shipping.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
